reason: The section states the vesting effect of recording a will for devised real estate.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registered will vesting effect on devised real estate

focusSelections.evidenceText: recording of the will has the effect of vesting any real estate devised by the will

proposedGroups.reason: The rule also keeps the real estate subject to the Probate Court Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the vesting effect of recording a will for devised real estate.

reason: The target automatically vests undisposed estate property in those beneficially entitled after two years.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Automatic vesting of undisposed estate property after two years

focusSelections.evidenceText: not disposed of by the personal representatives

proposedGroups.reason: The property listed includes money, securities, personal chattels, and real property not disposed of, conveyed, divided, or distributed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when undisposed estate property vests without conveyance.

The target states the temporal scope of Part II by date of death.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application of Part II by date of death

focusSelections.evidenceText: applies only in cases of death after May 1, 1951

proposedGroups.reason: The rule is limited to when Part II applies.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine whether Part II applies based on the date of death.

reason: The section combines a marital property definition with widow-share rules for different child scenarios.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Marital property definition for widow intestacy shares
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection defines the property concept used in the widow-share rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the marital property concept used in section 22.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Widow share when intestate leaves one child or children
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections assign marital property interests plus one-half or one-third of residue depending on number of children.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine the widow share when an intestate leaves one child or multiple children.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Widow share when a child predeceases leaving issue
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection treats a deceased child with living issue as living for the widow share calculation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the widow-share rule when a child has died leaving issue.

reason: The section directs per stirpes distribution among issue subject to widow rights.

proposedGroups.reason: The rule applies when an intestate dies leaving issue.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply per stirpes distribution among issue in intestacy.

reason: The target gives the estate to the widow when there is no issue.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Intestate leaving widow and no issue

focusSelections.evidenceText: leaving a widow but no issue

proposedGroups.reason: The rule assigns the estate to the widow.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the distribution when an intestate leaves a widow and no issue.

reason: The section gives the estate to parents when there is no widow or issue.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Intestate leaving no widow and no issue but a parent

focusSelections.evidenceText: father and mother in equal shares

proposedGroups.reason: If one parent is dead, the estate goes to the survivor.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine the parental distribution when no widow or issue remains.

reason: The target distributes to siblings and children of deceased siblings when closer relatives are absent.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Intestate leaving siblings or children of deceased siblings

focusSelections.evidenceText: brothers and sisters in equal shares

proposedGroups.reason: Children of a deceased brother or sister take the share their parent would have taken.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the sibling and niece-nephew-by-representation rule.

reason: The section distributes equally to nephews and nieces when the listed closer relatives are absent.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Intestate leaving only nephews and nieces

focusSelections.evidenceText: nephews and nieces in equal shares

proposedGroups.reason: The rule excludes representation in this scenario.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the distribution when only nephews and nieces remain in the listed family line.

reason: The target distributes to next of kin of equal consanguinity degree when the listed family members are absent.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Intestate leaving no listed immediate family

focusSelections.evidenceText: next of kin of equal degree of consanguinity

proposedGroups.reason: The rule requires equal distribution and excludes representation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine distribution to next of kin when no listed closer relatives remain.

reason: The section states how to count kindred degree and treats half-blood kindred equally in the same degree.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Computing degrees of kindred and half-blood inheritance

focusSelections.evidenceText: counting upward from the intestate to the nearest common ancestor and then downward

proposedGroups.reason: The rule also provides equal inheritance for half-blood kindred in the same degree.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Compute degrees of kindred and identify the half-blood inheritance rule.

reason: The target treats relatives conceived before death but born later as inheriting as if born during life and surviving.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Posthumous descendants and relatives in intestacy

focusSelections.evidenceText: begotten before his death but born thereafter

proposedGroups.reason: The rule applies to descendants and relatives of the intestate.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the inheritance rule for posthumous descendants and relatives.

reason: The advancement section has a hotchpot calculation rule plus valuation and proof rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Accounting for advancement to a child in whole intestacy
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection reckons the advanced portion as part of the distributable estate and adjusts or excludes the child share.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine how an advancement affects a child share in a wholly intestate estate.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set value by writing or time advanced and place the proof burden on the asserting person.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the valuation and proof rules for alleged advancement.

reason: The section directs property not disposed of by will into intestacy distribution.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Undisposed will property distributed as intestacy
proposedGroups.reason: The property is distributed as if the testator died intestate and left no other estate.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify how property not disposed of by will is distributed.
